summary: Mini-wave heartbeat suppression causing slot fragmentation and transient GPU shortages in dedicated pool
description: Issue summary: Beginning 2026-03-12 14:12 UTC, LuminaHealth's dedicated pool in us-west experienced repeated short-duration p99 latency spikes and failed allocations. Impact: customer reports 20-40% throughput degradation for batched routes and intermittent 504s for short-stream endpoints. This appears correlated with a burst pattern we have not characterized: a 'mini-wave' of many very short-lived streams (~200-800ms) that suppress allocator heartbeats and lead to slot fragmentation across the pool. Environment: Production dedicated pool (LuminaHealth reserve), us-west region. Timeline: 14:12 UTC - first observed; 14:15-14:30 multiple transient allocation timeouts; 14:30 mitigation attempts (rate-limit knob) reduced but did not eliminate p99 spikes. Customer impact: degraded throughput and small number of user-facing errors during peak window.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Use dedicated tenant with small-stream fanout pattern (many sub-2000 token short streams) targeting batched route.
2) Simulate high short-stream churn (350-800ms sessions) across 200 concurrent connections.
3) Observe allocator slot locking, increased attach latency, and eviction/re-attach churn in serving runtime.
4) Monitor p99 token latency, GPU slot availability and allocator heartbeat gaps.
logs: 2026-03-12T14:12:08Z ERROR serving-runtime: attach-timeout tenant=LuminaHealth route=batches attach_ms=10234
investigation_notes: Initial hypothesis: burst of very short streams is preventing allocator heartbeats from making progress and causing fractional slot holds. The allocator considers many ephemeral connections as active, preventing efficient packing and causing slot fragmentation.
Telemetry: spike in short_stream_count metric (x7 baseline) from 14:10-14:22 UTC. Attach latency 95th rose from 120ms -> 9.8s. GPU slot free count dropped by ~30% for 90s windows.
Confirmed noise symptoms: background snapshotter not implicated, kernel logs show no driver OOMs. No node restarts in cluster window.
Reproduced in staging by replaying traffic fuzz: when short_stream_ratio > 60% we see allocator heartbeat miss and re-attach churn.

Triage: autoscaler temporarily suppressed scale-ups due to telemetry drop (autoscaler assumed noisy telemetry -> avoid oscillation). This prevented additional GPUs from attaching and prolonged degraded throughput.
Correlated with tenant's new client-side SDK change that converts long requests into many small parallel calls (customer-side change noted in support exchange).
comments: 2026-03-12T15:01 - Support (Ava Kim): Notified LuminaHealth CS contact about interim mitigation: reduce concurrency or enable short-stream bypass flag. Requested traffic samples and SDK version.
2026-03-12T15:35 - LuminaHealth (J. Patel): We deployed SDK v2.10 which introduced parallel sub-requests. Attached sample traces and verbose client timings.

2026-03-12T16:20 - SRE (Diego Martinez): Instrumented additional allocator logs and increased allocator debug level on reserved pool. Observed repeated lease holds by connections that closed before prefetch completed.
2026-03-13T09:12 - Infra (Maya Singh): We pushed a throttling rule that groups short-streams into a capped queue length; early test reduced attach-ms 95th from 9.8s to 1.2s in canary.

2026-03-14T10:02 - Product (Liam O'Connor): Recommend a short-term customer-facing mitigation (client-side serializing or enabling short-stream bypass) and medium-term change to allocator fairness heuristic.
2026-03-14T12:00 - SRE (Diego Martinez): Running extended canary across 3 reserved pods. Monitoring for regression after rolling throttling config to full pool.
root_cause_summary: Allocator heartbeat suppression triggered by extremely high ratio of short-lived streams; autoscaler suppressed scale-up due to telemetry drop, amplifying GPU scarcity. Combined effect caused slot fragmentation and transient GPU shortages for the dedicated tenant.
resolution: In progress - Applied a temporary throttling/aggregation rule in the dedicated pool that caps concurrent short streams per tenant and groups them to reduce attach churn. Requested LuminaHealth to roll back or stagger SDK parallelization as short-term customer mitigation. Longer-term: engineering will adjust allocator heuristics to detect short-stream patterns and prefer packing evictable ephemeral connections, and change autoscaler to use alternate telemetry during short-stream spikes.
follow_up_actions: 1) Engineering task: allocator heuristic R&D - add short-stream detection and fast-path packing (owner: Diego Martinez) - target ETA 2026-04-02.
2) Autoscaler change: fallback telemetry during short-stream telemetry drops (owner: Maya Singh) - target ETA 2026-04-09.
3) Customer success: coordinate LuminaHealth SDK mitigation plan and confirm rollback/stagger by 2026-03-18 (owner: Priya Rao).
4) Post-incident: create runbook section for 'short-stream mini-wave' patterns and recommended mitigations.
